params.commentary:
The ships come back. So does the risk.

The Rockit Manifest, Voyage 002. The full 16-page edition is out:

01 / Suez: Drewry counted 57 container ships through the canal in the week to 15 November, up 73% on a year earlier. Gemini (Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd) moves three more Asia–Europe loops to Suez from 4 December.

02 / Red Sea: the Houthis now hold Yemen's Red Sea coast and told ships to leave Saudi ports on 20 November. Bab el-Mandeb transits fell 28% from their October peak.

03 / Rates: Asia–Med was the only main lane to rise. Xeneta Far East–Med spot +6.8% to $4,989/40ft. December FAKs to the East Med are filed at $6,500–6,800, and Maersk's $1,500 Med peak surcharge applies from today.

04 / Air: global rates $3.45/kg, +31% year on year; Middle East–Europe +66%.

05 / Egypt: an IMF staff-level deal puts about $2.3bn on the table, pending the Board; the dollar was back above EGP 54 on 22 November.

Our read: book December Asia cargo early, and get the peak, fuel, piracy and Suez surcharges named in writing.

Read it online, every figure sourced:
